{{nihongo|'''Kirishima Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hyūga Province]].

{{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kirishima, Kagoshima|en|Kirishima, Kagoshima|qid=Q858352|lt=Kirishima|1=Kirishima, Kagoshima}}, {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|qid=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture|1=Kagoshima Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}.

{{ill|Takachiho-gawara|en|Takachiho-gawara|qid=Q10566710|lt=Takachiho-gawara|1=Takachiho-gawara}} the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="env.go.jp">{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}}</ref>

Historically, the entire of {{ill|Mount Kirishima|en|Mount Kirishima|qid=Q1319361|lt=Mount Kirishima|1=Mount Kirishima}} is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds.

It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], {{ill|Toyotama-hime|en|Toyotama-hime|qid=Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime|1=Toyotama-hime}}, [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Properties|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}, such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] [[:en:Eruption|Eruption]]s.

==Overview==

'''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|qid=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture|1=Kagoshima Prefecture}}. It is a designated {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012</ref>

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:<ref>[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website]</ref>
; Main deity
:* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]]
; Deities enshrined together
:* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]]
:* {{ill|Toyotama-hime|en|Toyotama-hime|qid=Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime no mikoto|1=Toyotama-hime}}
:* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]]
:* {{ill|Tamayori-hime|en|Tamayori-hime|qid=Q56344982|lt=Tamayori-hime no mikoto|1=Tamayori-hime}}
:* {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Jinmu-tenno|1=Emperor Jimmu}}

== History ==
[[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]]
[[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]]
According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater {{ill|Otake|en|Otake|qid=Q7108397|lt=Otake|1=Otake}}, known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}</ref> Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}</ref>

Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[:en:Tenson Korin|Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.<ref></ref>

The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in {{ill|940|en|940|qid=Q23830|lt=940|1=940}} or {{ill|950|en|950|qid=Q23449|lt=950|1=950}} by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions.<ref name=":0" />

In {{ill|1234|en|1234|qid=Q5424|lt=1234|1=1234}}, another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later.<ref name=":0" />

In {{ill|1484|en|1484|qid=Q6639|lt=1484|1=1484}}, the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[:en:Shimazu Tadamasa|Shimazu Tadamasa]].<ref name=":0" /> The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in {{ill|1715|en|1715|qid=Q6884|lt=1715|1=1715}} by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]].<ref name=":0" />

Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}}</ref> Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.<ref></ref>

The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the {{ill|Battle of Mimigawa|en|Battle of Mimigawa|qid=Q4871739|lt=Battle of Mimigawa|1=Battle of Mimigawa}} in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.<ref></ref>

[[:en:Sakamoto Ryoma|Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.<ref>Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}}</ref>

Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.<ref></ref> In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system.

On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.<ref>{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}</ref>

The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.<ref></ref>

== festivals ==
Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu.
* Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month
* Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month
* Saitan-sai - January 1
* Hatsuniku-sai - January 2
* Genshi-sai - January 3
* Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year)
* Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4)
* Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June
* Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31
* Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August
* festival - September 19
* Joyasai - December 31

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Treasures ===
* Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.</ref>.

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor)
* Chokushiden
(In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties)
* Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings)
* Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building)
<gallery>
File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view)
File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden
File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor
</gallery>
These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West."

== Precincts ==
The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the {{ill|Abolition of the han system|en|Abolition of the han system|qid=Q331905|lt=Abolition of the han system|1=Abolition of the han system}} in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|en|Constitution of Japan|qid=Q237082|lt=Constitution of Japan|1=Constitution of Japan}} in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.<ref>Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992.</ref>

</gallery>

{{nihongo|'''Kirishima Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hyūga Province]].

'''Kirishima Shrine'' (Kirishima Shrine) is located in {{ill|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701|qid=Q15701|1=Kagoshima Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Kirishima City|Q858352|qid=Q858352|1=Kirishima, Kagoshima}}Kirishima Taguchi. It is {{ill|lt=Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904|1=Shikinai Ronsha}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishikinaisha|1=UNKNOWN}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=old company rank|1=UNKNOWN}} is {{ill|lt=Modern company rank system #government shrine|Q712534|qid=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}<ref name="Shrine Agency">[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Shrine] - Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency February 27, 2012</ref>. The main shrine, shrine hall, and worship hall are designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|qid=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 9 dated February 9, 2020. </ref>.

=== Enshrined God ===
The following seven deities are currently enshrined <ref>[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html History] (official website). </ref>.
; Main enshrined deity
:* {{ill|lt=Ninigi|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Tenraoseki Kokuroseki Amatsu Hidakahiko Fire Qiong Qionggi|1=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}
; Aidenjin

=== History ===
[[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Old Palace]]
[[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred Cedar]]
During the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|qid=Q329792|1=Emperor Kinmei}} (6th century), a monk named Keitane Shonin visited {{ill|lt=Takachihomine|Q3514128|qid=Q3514128|1=Mount Takachiho}}. {{ill|lt=Ohachi|Q11489346|qid=Q11489346|lt=It is said that the shrine building was built on Setao (Setao Hill) between Hijomine (Ohachi)|1=Ohachi}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture |date=1983-03-08 |year=1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}</ref>. One theory is that it was founded in the first year of {{ill|lt=Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|qid=Q329792|1=Emperor Kinmei}} ({{ill|lt=540|Q30900|qid=Q30900|1=540}}). |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}</ref>.{{ill|lt=Takachihomine|Q3514128|qid=Q3514128|1=Mount Takachiho}} is said to be the place where {{ill|lt=descendance of the descendants of the descendants of the descendants of heaven|Q1084733|qid=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}} in Japanese mythology, so the gods associated with {{ill|lt=three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075|qid=Q56347075|1=Three generations of Hyuga}} are currently enshrined there. However, it is thought that this shrine originally began as a {{ill|lt=mountain cult|Q93697439|qid=Q93697439|1=Mountain worship}}, where {{ill|lt=mountain worship|Q93697439|qid=Q93697439|1=Mountain worship}} worshiped {{ill|lt=Takachihomine|Q3514128|qid=Q3514128|1=Mount Takachiho}} itself.

The original shrine, Setao, was located close to the crater, so the shrine often caught fire due to eruptions, and was destroyed in the eruption of {{ill|lt=Ohachi|Q11489346|qid=Q11489346|lt=Hōjomine (Ohachi)|1=Ohachi}} in July of {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} ({{ill|lt=788|Q30721|qid=Q30721|1=788}}).After that, {{ill|lt=Tenkei|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340|1=Tengyō}}3 years ({{ill|lt=940|Q23830|qid=Q23830|1=940}}) or {{ill|lt=Tenryaku|Q1346281|qid=Q1346281|1=Tenryaku}}4 during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Murakami|Q374015|qid=Q374015|1=Emperor Murakami}} In the year ({{ill|lt=950|Q23449|qid=Q23449|1=950}}), it was rebuilt in Setaogoe (currently {{ill|lt=Takachiho River|Q10566710|qid=Q10566710|1=Takachiho-gawara}}, old palace ruins) by {{ill|lt=Sekora|Q11491623|qid=Q11491623|1=Shōkū}} Shonin, but this place has also been rebuilt many times. In the first year of {{ill|lt=Bunryaku|Q1194125|qid=Q1194125|1=Bunryaku}} ({{ill|lt=1234|Q5424|qid=Q5424|1=1234}}), the large eruption of {{ill|lt=Ohachi|Q11489346|qid=Q11489346|lt=Kajomine (Ohachi)|1=Ohachi}} caused the shrine buildings, monk's quarters, etc. was completely destroyed by fire, so a "temporary shrine" was built at Tachiyo in Kirishima Taguchi (next to Kirishima Junior High School, bordering the {{ill|lt=Kirishima Town|Q6415332|qid=Q6415332|1=Kirishima, Kagoshima (town)}} ground), where it was worshiped for about 250 years.<ref name=":0" />.{{ill|lt=Civilization_(Japan)|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Civilization|1=Bunmei}} In 16 years ({{ill|lt=1484|Q6639|qid=Q6639|1=1484}}), Kenkei Shonin rebuilt the current Kirishima Shrine on the orders of {{ill|lt=Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874|qid=Q11162874|1=Shimazu Tadamasa}}. However, the shrine building went up in flames many times after that, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in 1715|Q6884}} by {{ill|lt=Yoshitaka Shimazu|Q11246537|qid=Q11246537|1=Shimazu Yoshitaka}} as a dedication.

Another theory is that after the shrine building was destroyed by an eruption in the first year of {{ill|lt=Bunryaku|Q1194125|qid=Q1194125|1=Bunryaku}} ({{ill|lt=1234|Q5424|qid=Q5424|1=1234}}), the shrine building was moved to Mt. Nagao (the current location of Higashi Kirishima Shrine) east of {{ill|lt=Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361|qid=Q1319361|1=Mount Kirishima}}. (Japan)|Q1193544|Bunmei}} In 16 years ({{ill|lt=1484|Q6639|qid=Q6639|1=1484}}), {{ill|lt=Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874|qid=Q11162874|1=Shimazu Tadamasa}} called it "Tosha" ('''Kirishima It is said that it was divided into two shrines: Higashi Gozaisho Gongen''' (currently 'Kirishima Higashi Shrine') and 'West Shrine' ('''Nishi Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen''', currently 'Kirishima Jingu''').<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary |date=1997-09-25 |year=1997 |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing}}</ref>.In addition to this, after moving the shrine building to Mt. Nagao to the east of {{ill|lt=Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361|qid=Q1319361|1=Mount Kirishima}}, the current '''{{ill|lt=Kirishima Shrine|Q11660876|qid=Q11660876|1=Kirishimamine Shrine}}'' and '''Mist There is also a theory that it was divided into two shrines, ``Shimahigashi Shrine'' and ``Kirishimanishi Shrine'' (currently ``Kirishima Jingu'') from ``Kirishimahigashi Shrine''.

Respected by the successive {{ill|lt=Shimazu clan|Q1061406|qid=Q1061406|1=Shimazu clan}}, {{ill|lt=Yoshihisa Shimazu|Q955727|qid=Q955727|1=Shimazu Yoshihisa}} was born in {{ill|lt=Tensho|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}}6 ({{ill|lt=15 In 1978|Q6707|qid=Q6707|1=1578}}) {{ill|lt=Battle of Mimikawa|Q4871739|qid=Q4871739|1=Battle of Mimigawa}}, he visited a shrine and drew a {{ill|lt=lottery|Q5433694|qid=Q5433694|lt=a wig|1=demarchy}}, and also in 14th year of Tensho (1978) when he moved north to Kyushu. {{ill|lt=1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736|1=1585}}) In June, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yontaka Zenyabo|1=UNKNOWN}} of Sosaki Tatsucho and his senior retainer {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Arinobu Yamada|1=UNKNOWN}} and again in September, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kiyōyoshi Yoshida|1=UNKNOWN}}, respectively, to draw the wig and decide on the direction of the invasion.He often seeks divine counsel when making important decisions.{{Source required|date=February 2022}}.It is also known that {{ill|lt=Ryoma Sakamoto|Q378450|qid=Q378450|1=Sakamoto Ryōma}} visited the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kirishima Mountain Range|1=UNKNOWN}} on what is said to be Japan's first honeymoon, but by that time he was already at the top of the mountain. <ref>Ryoma Sakamoto{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|New character old kana|Letter - December 4, Keio 2, addressed to Otome Sakamoto-}}</ref>.

Until the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Ordinance|1=UNKNOWN}} was issued during the Meiji period, it was called ``West Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen,'' and the main hall was an eleven-faced Kannon. It has Karinji Temple in Bettoji Temple. It played a central role in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kirishima Rokusho Gongen|1=UNKNOWN}} worship by Shugen monks centered on Mt. Kirishima.{{Citation required|date=February 2022}}.
Under the {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|qid=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, in February 1874|Q7761}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}), it was ranked as {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|qid=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.

{{ill|lt=1935|Q18658|qid=Q18658|1=1935}} (1935) {{ill|lt=November 16|Q3029|qid=Q3029|1=November 16}}, after {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Special Army Exercise|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|qid=Q34479|1=Hirohito}} {{ill|lt=Yukiyuki|Q11626055|qid=Q11626055|1=Imperial visits}}<ref>{{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Takeshi Hara |title=Complete record of Emperor Showa's train |publisher=Shinchosha |date=2016-09-30 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}</ref>.Also, the {{ill|lt=sacred tree|Q48743901|qid=Q48743901|1=Shinboku}} {{ill|lt=cedar|Q147388|qid=Q147388|lt=cedar|1=Cryptomeria}} is estimated to be about 800 years old, and is said to be the ancestor of the cedars of southern Kyushu {{citation needed|date=February 2022}}.

According to a government report on February 9, 2020, the "Honden, Heiden, and Worship Hall" were designated as national treasures <ref>[https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-kirishima.html Kirishima City Official Homepage Overview of Designated Cultural Properties [Kirishima]]</ref>.

=== Rituals ===
Approximately 100 rituals are held annually.
* Tsukutachisai (first day of every month)
* Monthly Festival (Tsukinamisai) 19th of every month
* Saitan Festival January 1st
* Hatsunikkusai (January 2nd)
* Genshi Festival January 3rd
* Uchimaki Festival February 18th (January 1st in the lunar calendar)
* Rice planting festival March 3rd (February 4th in the lunar calendar)
* Sanada's Nagata Rice Planting Festival (Sanada's Osada Otauesai) First Sunday of June
* Great Purification Ceremony June 30th, December 31st
* Minamikyushu Kagura Last Saturday of August
* Regular festival September 19th
* New Year's Eve Festival December 31st

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
* 1 main hall, 1 hall of worship, and 2 attached building tags (buildings) - Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4).

=== Important cultural property ===
* Climbing corridor
* Imperial Envoy Hall
(The following is designated as “attached”)
* Kadomori Shrine 2 buildings
* 1 sacred food hall
<gallery>
File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Imperial Envoy Hall (side)
File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Shrine of Worship
File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Noboriro
</gallery>
The shrine building mentioned above was donated by the Kagoshima feudal lord {{ill|lt=Yoshiki Shimazu|Q11246537|qid=Q11246537|1=Shimazu Yoshitaka}} and was built in 1715. The shrine buildings are all ornately painted in vermilion. The interior of the main hall in particular is luxuriously decorated, with pillars, beams, and long pillars all painted with vermilion lacquer, important points decorated with colored patterns and plated decorative metal fittings, and walls decorated with panels with richly colored reliefs. {{ill|lt=Shinto architecture|Q3080012|qid=Q3080012|1=Shinto architecture}} It is rare to find such elaborate decorations not only on the outside but also on the inside, and it has another name: ``Nikko of the West''.

=== Precincts ===
Originally, the {{ill|lt=Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361|qid=Q1319361|1=Mount Kirishima}} area was the precincts of Kirishima Shrine, but in 1871|Q7746}}, {{j alink|Abolition of feudal domains|Q331905}} Prefectural borders were drawn along the top of Mt. Kirishima, and the {{ill|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300|qid=Q130300|1=Miyazaki Prefecture}} side was excluded from the shrine precincts. In Meiji 15 ({{ill|lt=1882|Q7812|qid=Q7812|1=1882}}), the area was further reduced by 7,810 hectares, and in {{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|qid=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}21 ({{ill|lt=1946|Q18610|qid=Q18610|1=1946}}), most of the forest became state-owned land with the enactment of the {{ill|lt=Constitution of Japan|Q237082|qid=Q237082|1=Constitution of Japan}}, which turned it into a religious corporation. Later, 789 hectares needed for festival events were returned to the shrine.<ref>Kirishima Town Local History, edited by Kirishima Town Local History Editorial Committee, Kirishima Town, 1992. </ref>.
